neighbours.label: the word marking how far an age or life-stage span extends ('until age five', 'up to the age of', 'throughout adult life', 'from three months to four years'); the same prepositions for space, weekdays or giving stay quiet. The - pole marks the START of such a span ('begin', 'as early as')
fire: Babies should sleep in the parents' room until about six months of age.
The vaccine protects children from infancy throughout their school years.
She wore glasses from early childhood until she was nearly thirty.
The scheme covers young people from age sixteen until their twenty-fifth birthday.
Bone density keeps rising in adolescence and continues until the late twenties.
He stuttered badly as a boy and throughout his teenage years.
The nursery takes infants from six weeks until they turn three.
Most puppies keep their milk teeth until around four months old.
quiet: Babies can begin eating solid food at about six months of age.
The bus runs from the station through the old town to the harbour.
She walked from the kitchen to the garden with a cup of tea.
Young people can begin the scheme as early as age sixteen.
Keep stirring the sauce until it thickens and coats the spoon.
He handed the keys to his brother and left for the airport.
The nursery is closed until the heating has been repaired.
Most puppies already have milk teeth at around four weeks old.

notes: Card: ' until' x8, ' through' x5, ' to' x4, ' throughout', ' hasta'; every top example is about ages or life stages (until 1 year of age, up to age 6, three months to four years, throughout our entire lives). Probes: 'throughout adult life' 0.87, 'from birth until age five' 0.66, 'up to the age of twelve' 0.22, 'Monday through Friday' 0.20, 'June to September' 0.14; 'through the door', 'to his sister', 'until the paint is dry', 'from the harbour to the church' < 0.04; 'as early as age three' -0.003 (that is the - pole: ' as', ' begin', ' déjà'). One distinction, two sides: + = span runs up to/through here, - = span starts here.
